definition: Machine learning with multi-layer neural networks that learn hierarchical representations from raw data.
details: By stacking many layers, deep networks compose simple features into increasingly abstract ones — edges into parts, parts into objects — with the representations learned from data rather than engineered. Combined with large datasets and fast GPUs, this approach reset the state of the art across speech, vision, translation and games.

explainer.lead: Deep learning lets computers discover useful patterns by passing data through many connected layers, rather than relying on people to design every feature by hand. With large datasets and fast GPUs, it has produced major advances in speech, vision, translation, and games.

tiers.eli5: Imagine learning to recognize a dog by first noticing lines, then spotting ears and legs, and finally putting those clues together. Deep learning works in a similar way: each layer builds on the clues found by the layer before it. It learns these clues from examples instead of being given a hand-written checklist.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners train multi-layer neural networks on raw inputs, using large datasets and GPU acceleration to learn hierarchical features for tasks such as vision, speech, and translation. The approach reduces manual feature engineering, but its strong results depend on having suitable data and substantial computation.
tiers.paperLevel: A deep network composes many learned transformations, schematically f(x) = f_L(...f_2(f_1(x))...), so successive layers represent increasingly abstract features. Its parameters and representations are learned from data rather than manually engineered. The stated gains across speech, vision, translation, and games rely on large datasets and fast GPUs.

explainer.example: For an image-recognition task, raw pixels enter the network; early layers learn edges, middle layers combine edges into parts, and later layers combine parts into an object representation used to recognize the image.

usedIn.name: Computer vision
usedIn.detail: Learns visual features that progress from edges to object parts and whole objects.

usedIn.name: Speech recognition
usedIn.detail: Uses learned multi-layer representations to advance the state of the art in speech tasks.

usedIn.name: Machine translation
usedIn.detail: Learns representations directly from translation data instead of relying entirely on engineered features.

usedIn.name: Games
usedIn.detail: Applies deep neural networks to learn useful representations for game playing.

explainer.intuition: A deep network builds understanding in stages: early layers capture simple patterns, and later layers combine them into more abstract and useful representations.
howItWorks: Feed raw data into the first layer of a neural network.
Let early layers learn simple features, such as edges in an image.
Pass those features through more layers that combine them into parts and then objects.
Learn the entire hierarchy from training data rather than hand-engineering each feature.
Use the final representation to produce the task's output.
explainer.whyItMatters: Learning representations directly from raw data removes much of the need for manual feature design. Together with large datasets and fast GPUs, this reset the state of the art in several major fields.
misconceptions: Deep learning is not simply feature engineering with more layers: its representations are learned from data.
Stacking layers alone does not explain its practical success; large datasets and fast GPUs are also central.
